study type: Longitudinal secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial
outcome: Mother-infant sharing of viral and plasmid strains
cohort: The study participants were 28 mother-infant dyads where all infants were delivered by cesarean section.
finding: The infant gut mobilome (virome and plasmidome) increases in richness over the first 6 postnatal weeks, demonstrating high individual-specificity and temporal stability, with formula-fed infants exhibiting greater mobilome richness than breastfed infants, and plasmid composition influenced by antibiotic exposure and birth weight.
mod_finding: N/A (The study exclusively included cesarean-born infants, so no comparative findings related to mode of birth are presented).
followup_time: Up to 6 months of age (for mother-infant sharing).
birth_weight: Birth weight was measured and found to influence plasmid composition.
